crosswalks.label: Web Developers
crosswalks.rationale: Web Developers directly cover web applications, application databases, interfaces, browser/device compatibility, performance and integration, but do not equal every full-stack role.

crosswalks.label: Software Developers
crosswalks.rationale: Software Developers cover software solutions, interfaces, performance and hardware/software integration; full-stack is a bounded specialization inside broader software work.

findings.summary: O*NET occupational evidence provides a human-work baseline for the core tasks adjacent to Full-Stack Engineer; AXM keeps the mapping bounded instead of treating the occupation code as profession identity.
findings.rationale: The candidate body includes the grounded core while preserving narrower AXM ownership boundaries.

findings.summary: Make cross-layer convenience explicitly subordinate to Frontend, Backend, Database, Security, SRE and Product ownership so full-stack execution cannot become default institutional authority.
method_labels: O*NET occupation comparison plus AXM body-boundary review
findings.rationale: The external occupation is broader or differently bundled, so explicit separation is required before reusable package composition.

gaps_against_body.description: Make cross-layer convenience explicitly subordinate to Frontend, Backend, Database, Security, SRE and Product ownership so full-stack execution cannot become default institutional authority.

nonclaims: This packet does not claim complete reconstruction of Full-Stack Engineer.
The O*NET occupation mapping is evidence for human work structure, not AXM profession identity or automatic scope transfer.
No TEST, WORKING, CANON, product, security, safety, legal or institutional authority is created by this research packet.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: This research packet creates no execution, institutional, legal, safety, security, product, or certification authority.
